thread:
Asha: Quick async check-in — day 3 onboarding. What I did: received laptop, installed devenv, VPN connected, verified schedular demo app runs locally. Blockers: still getting 403 on push to gitlab, `kubectl` has no context for the dev cluster, and MFA sometimes times out when I approve on my phone. Today: try SSH key regen, follow up with infra, start a tiny PR to exercise CI. TL;DR: almost there but need the final infra bits.

Ben: Thanks Asha — welcome! Can you paste the output of these two commands so I can forward to infra?
`gcloud auth list`
`kubectl config current-context`

Asha: Paste below — threw in minimal logs.
```
$ gcloud auth list
Credentialed accounts:
 - asha@example.com (active)

$ kubectl config current-context
error: current-context is not set
```

Priya: Hey — I'm on infra. I can see a denied push attempt in the audit logs for asha@example.com. Two quick checks: 1) did you add your SSH public key to GitLab profile (User Settings > SSH Keys)? 2) Are you trying HTTPS or SSH remote? `git remote -v` will show.

Asha: Using SSH. `git remote -v` output: `origin git@git.redwood.example:team/repo.git (fetch)`

Priya: Ok looks right. I added your account to the `dev-developers` group just now — give it ~30s and try `ssh -T git@git.redwood.example` then `git push`. If still 403, paste `ssh -vvv` output. Also I'll add you to the kubeconfig for `dev-us-west` cluster.

infra-bot: SSO login event for asha@example.com succeeded (idp:saml-okta) at 2026-03-17T15:02:11Z.

Asha: Ran `ssh -T` — got `Welcome to GitLab, @asha!` Tried push, still 403 on protected branch. I'll make a branch and push to tests branch. Also got updated kubeconfig from Priya and `kubectl config current-context` now shows `dev-us-west`.

Ben: For MFA timeouts — do you have the Okta Verify app and device time synced? Sometimes phone clock drift causes push prompts to fail. Also try the hardware token fallback if you have it.

Asha: Re-synced phone clock, re-added SSH key (copied from `~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub`) and retried. Push to my feature branch succeeded. I can `kubectl get pods` in dev cluster now. One remaining tiny thing: CI job is failing with `pip: cannot find header for libffi` while building a wheel. Will try to `apt-get install libffi-dev` in the container locally, otherwise pinging infra for the build image fix.

Priya: Good progress — I pushed a temporary image rebuild to include libffi-dev in the build stage; CI should pick it up on next pipeline run.

Asha: Awesome — pipeline passed. No more blockers. Going to open a WIP PR and start reading the docs page on canary rollouts. Thanks for the quick help :raised_hands:
